definitions.explanation: Feeding on plants and vegetation. Used to describe animals that eat only plants.

In modern slang, describes a person (especially a man) who is passive and unassertive, particularly in romantic relationships. From the term {草食|そうしょく}{系|けい}{男子|だんし} (herbivore man), coined in the mid-2000s.

examples.japanese: ⟦{牛|うし}→牛：01857_ushi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{草食|そうしょく}⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧だ。
{草食|そうしょく}⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{植物|しょくぶつ}→植物：03248_shokubutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べて→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦{生活|せいかつ}する→生活する：01839_seikatsusuru⟧。
examples.english: Herbivorous animals live by eating plants.

examples.japanese: ⟦{恐竜|きょうりゅう}→恐竜：10428_kyouryuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{草食|そうしょく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧もの⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{肉食|にくしょく}→肉食：13922_nikushoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ものがいた。

⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{草食|そうしょく}⟦{男子|だんし}→男子：03425_danshi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えた→増える：01183_fueru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。

examples.english: Men of the 'herbivore' type tend to be seen as passive in romance.

notes:
Has both a biological meaning (herbivorous) and a widely known modern slang meaning (passive/unassertive person). The slang usage comes from the buzzword {草食|そうしょく}{系|けい}⟦{男子|だんし}→男子：03425_danshi⟧ ('herbivore man'), coined around 2006 to describe young men who are not aggressively pursuing romantic or sexual relationships.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {草食|そうしょく}⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧: herbivore, herbivorous animal
- {草食|そうしょく}{系|けい}: herbivore type (slang for passive person)
- {草食|そうしょく}⟦{男子|だんし}→男子：03425_danshi⟧: herbivore man — passive, unassertive man
- {草食|そうしょく}⟦{女子|じょし}→女子：03350_joshi⟧: herbivore woman — passive, unassertive woman

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{肉食|にくしょく}→肉食：13922_nikushoku⟧: carnivorous — in slang, aggressive and assertive in romance
- ⟦{雑食|ざっしょく}→雑食：20418_zasshoku⟧: omnivorous — eating both plants and meat
